actions.title: Falsifying Reward Scalarization Assumptions

assumptions: Scalarization weights are the primary bottleneck in non-stationary multi-objective environments.
Environmental goals shift over time, necessitating weight adaptation.
definition.falsification: No statistically significant difference in performance metrics between agents utilizing static scalarization and those utilizing dynamic weight adjustment in the specified test environment.
definition.statement: Dynamic adjustment of scalarization weights, when modulated by environmental feedback, significantly improves Pareto-optimal policy convergence in non-stationary multi-objective environments compared to static scalarization.
definition.uncertainty: The specific scheduling function for weight adaptation in non-stationary environments remains undefined and requires empirical optimization.

definition.reason: Hypothesis (hyp-assump-test-02) provides a testable framework; retrieval of further sources is secondary to empirical validation of the performance contrast.
definition.stop: Measurement validity across 3 distinct random seeds.
definition.uncertainty: Whether the simulation environment captures sufficient non-stationarity to differentiate the scalarization methods.
